name: Russia
gaps: Specific regional club websites for most BirdsRussia branches are not individually maintained online; activity concentrated in Moscow region and through national platforms. Several historical Russian ornithological sites may be offline or defunct since 2022.
A separate "Birdwatching Moscow" Facebook link was dropped: it pointed to the same page as BirdsRussia, already listed, not a distinct community.

groups.name: BirdsRussia
groups.blurb: National ornithological society with eleven regional branches running field research and conservation across Russia.

groups.name: Russian Ornithological Society
groups.blurb: Regional ornithological association from Saint Petersburg running bird rehabilitation and conservation activities.

groups.name: Ru-Birds platform
groups.blurb: Online bird observation database for ornithologists and birders to share sightings and data from across Russia.

groups.name: Birds of Siberia
groups.blurb: Birding platform for rare birds and birdwatching reports from Irkutsk, Yakutia and Lake Baikal regions.

name: Ukraine
gaps: Regional office details for USPB branches are partially available on main site but individual regional club websites are limited. Some western regions (Transcarpathia, Lviv) have informal local guide networks rather than formal club websites.

groups.name: USPB / BirdLife Ukraine
groups.blurb: Ukrainian Society for the Protection of Birds, BirdLife partner since 1994 with regional branches and conservation work.

groups.name: Birds of Ukraine
groups.blurb: Ukraine's largest bird photo database and communication hub for birdwatchers with species records and checklists.

groups.name: Birdwatching Ukraine
groups.blurb: Facebook community of birdwatchers and ornithologists sharing observations and birding news across Ukraine.

name: Belarus
gaps: Belarus Ornitho-Faunistic Commission is a member of the European Rarities Committees but no independent public website found. BirdLife Belarus (APB) was dissolved by government in 2022. Current organized birding communities are limited; most activity through informal birding networks and tourism operators.

groups.name: Belovezhskaya Pushcha National Park
groups.blurb: UNESCO World Heritage site and key ornithological area monitoring over 250 bird species including rare raptors.

groups.name: Birding Belarus
groups.blurb: Facebook community sharing rare bird sightings and birding observations across Belarus.

name: Moldova
gaps: Society for Birds and Nature Protection (SPPN) lacks a public website; contact via email sppn.moldova@gmail.com. No dedicated regional clubs or public birding communities found online. Organised birding primarily through national monitoring and tour operators.

groups.name: SPPN / Society for Birds and Nature Protection
groups.blurb: The national bird and nature protection society, with no site of its own; linked via the PECBMS monitoring page that credits them as Moldova's contributing partner.

name: Georgia
gaps: "Birding Caucasus" was dropped: it is a commercial birding tour agency, not a community, per the never include rule.

groups.name: SABUKO / Society for Nature Conservation
groups.blurb: BirdLife partner since 2013 running bird monitoring and conservation across Georgia's wetlands and mountains.

groups.name: Batumi Raptor Count
groups.blurb: Citizen science project monitoring one million migrating raptors each autumn at a key global migration bottleneck.

name: Armenia
gaps: A separate "Birding Armenia" Facebook link was dropped: the handle matched ASPB, already listed under its own site, not a distinct community.

groups.name: ASPB / Armenian Society for the Protection of Birds
groups.blurb: BirdLife partner managing Important Bird Areas and running bird conservation and monitoring across Armenia.

name: Azerbaijan
gaps: Azerbaijan Ornithological Society (AOS) website aos.az not currently accessible. Most organized activity through Birding Azerbaijan platform.

groups.name: Birding Azerbaijan
groups.blurb: Nonprofit sharing bird news, scientific research and birding opportunities with focus on Asian species and conservation.
